summary: Persistent 429s after enabling edge TLS 1.3 0-RTT (early-data) — duplicate token accounting
description:
Issue summary: Finstream Labs reported sudden, persistent 429 responses across low-latency chat routes shortly after we enabled TLS 1.3 0-RTT (early-data) on the edge in us-east. Impact: customer-facing production requests receiving 10-30% 429 rate on interactive routes for ~4 hours, causing degraded UX and increased retry amplification. Environment: Dedicated customer pool in prod (us-east primary, eu-west failover).

High-level hypothesis: early-data (0-RTT) requests were being accounted at two layers (accept-time accounting at the edge front-end and again at the application-layer request start) when session resumption / 0-RTT replay occurred, causing token-bucket double-debiting and exhausted burst credits for the tenant.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a client supporting TLS 1.3 0-RTT, establish a session then close and immediately re-open to get 0-RTT early-data resumption tokens.
2) Send many small interactive generation requests (50-200 concurrent short chat calls) with 0-RTT early-data enabled to the customer's dedicated route.
3) Observe returned 429s in ~15-35% of responses within the burst window; corresponding token/burst counters on the tenant drop faster than expected.
4) Repeat same workload with 0-RTT disabled — 429s disappear and token consumption aligns with expected per-token accounting.
logs: edge-proxy (us-east) tcp_accept.log: connection_id=abc123 accepted early_data=true tenant=finstream tokens_debited=1
api-gateway request.log: request_id=req-9a7 tenant=finstream start_counted=true tokens_debited=1
rate-limiter meter: tenant=finstream burst_balance went from 1200 -> 0 in 90s (expected ~800)
comments: 2024-11-20 10:12 — Support (Jasmine): Customer reports ~20% 429s on /v1/chat generate after yesterday's edge change; ticketing because UX severely impacted. Asked for request IDs and approximate start time.
2024-11-20 10:27 — SRE (Marco): Noted correlation with our edge flag rollout enabling TLS 1.3 0-RTT in us-east at 09:40 UTC. Added SRE on-call and put customer on priority queue.

2024-11-20 11:05 — SRE (Marco): Reproduced locally using curl with TLS 1.3 early data; saw two debit events for single logical request in internal test harness. Opening PR to edge-proxy to de-duplicate early-data accounting. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1823.

2024-11-21 02:00 — Support (Jasmine): Customer accepted temporary mitigation to disable 0-RTT for their tenant at edge config; 429s dropped to baseline immediately. Customer requested permanent fix timeline.

2024-11-22 09:30 — SRE (Marco): Hotfix deployed to us-east and eu-west edge clusters. Confirmed token accounting corrected and no further tenant 429 spikes. Marking resolved and documenting runbook change.
2024-11-22 10:02 — Customer (Finstream Platform Eng): Confirmed production traffic recovered and monitoring shows normal burst balance reclaim. Appreciated prioritization.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: 429s correlated tightly with edge flag rollout time window. No changes to rate-limiter logic in control-plane at that time.
Test reproduction: used OpenSSL s_client + curl to simulate 0-RTT early data; reproduced debit-on-accept + debit-on-request pattern in dedicated-pool tenant accounting logs.

Root cause: edge-proxy's TLS early-data path triggered pre-request 'ingress' accounting hook when a TCP session with early-data was accepted. The application-layer request parser also invoked the standard debit path when request headers were processed. No guard existed to mark early-data as "accounted" for the subsequent application layer, so both layers charged the token bucket.

Scope: affected only tenants on dedicated pools that had the edge 0-RTT flag enabled and used proxies that support session resumption/0-RTT. Public hosted customers unaffected because their fronting proxies have a different TLS stack.
Immediate mitigation validated: toggling edge TLS 0-RTT off for the tenant removed duplicate accounting and recovered burst balance instantly.

Fix approach: add idempotency marker on connection metadata when early-data accounting runs, and make application-layer debit path check-and-skip if marker present. Also add unit and integration tests simulating accept + 0-RTT replay.
resolution: Permanent fix merged and rolled out (edge-proxy PR #1823). Hotfix deployed to us-east and eu-west edge clusters on 2024-11-22 08:45 UTC. Steps: 1) Patch adds connection-level marker to prevent double-debit on early-data; 2) Integration tests added to CI harness; 3) Runbook updated to include a check for 0-RTT flag correlation when tenants see burst exhaustion. Customer's tenant had 0-RTT disabled during investigation; re-enabled after patch roll-out and monitored for 24h—no recurrence. Follow-up: add telemetry to surface early-data debit events in console (ENGINE-528), and schedule postmortem doc on Confluence.
